title: I Posted the Campground Fire-Ring Quiet Hours the Neighbor Ignored

parts.text: I banked coals at 10:02 p.m. and site 14 still had a full ring under the quiet sign. The post said: FIRES DOWN AT TEN. NO NEW LOGS. QUIET TO SEVEN. I was forty-six, permit holder, holding a site map. Neighbor Joss shrugged. "Camps are the night." I photographed the post, the map, and the new log. Then I asked for the ranger log. At 10:08 the ranger pinged why Joss's name was on a post-ten fire. I did not argue the joke. I argued the file. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The ranger can see Joss's new log on site 14 after quiet hours.

social.video_title: The neighbor added a log after the ten o'clock fire rule — Part 1/2
social.description: Campground, a quiet post, a full ring. I logged the log. Would you have asked the ranger?

parts.text: Joss called it ambience until the ranger asked for the still. I printed the log, the post, and the photo. The fire banked. Joss sat dark and told the next site ambience was always about optics. Optics is a word neighbors use when posts exist. Quiet hours now have a second line: LOGS STOP AT TEN. I keep the map. Joss brown-bags the jokes. The ring finally looks like a permit, not a party. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Ranger log, banked coals, and a second line. Was ambience ever post-ten?
